The restart phase's outcome is therefore attributable to the target rather than to missing transport wiring.

scope.description: One two-voter cluster of real nodes over in-memory transports. The leading member's log store fails exactly the write carrying the configuration entry that would remove the other voter. The harness records the configuration index the leader holds afterwards against its last stored log index, then waits for the node to lead again and applies one client command, comparing the resulting commit index with the other voter's last log index. The successor additionally restarts the phantom leader from its own stores after the lone commit and records restart success, whether it regains leadership, whether the commit remains in its log, and whether the peer's log has reached that index. In this revision the restarted node's transport is wired to the surviving peer in both directions before the election window, so the restart outcome reflects the target.
assumptions: Both members run the captured code with 300 ms heartbeat, election and lease timeouts and share no state.
The injected failure is a single StoreLogs call returning an error; the store is otherwise the standard in-memory store and accepts later writes.
The harness does not assert which of the two members becomes leader first; it targets whichever one leads when the failure is injected.
A command is treated as committed when its Apply future returns nil, which is the client-visible completion point.
excluded: No restart of the failed node, so the log-derived configuration that would replace the phantom one is not exercised.
No snapshot, no third member and no concurrent client traffic.

basis.prefix: The harness creates two in-memory transports connected to each other, bootstraps the same two-voter configuration on both stores, and starts both rafts with 300 ms timeouts. It waits for a leader, arms that leader's log store to fail the next StoreLogs call, and calls RemoveServer for the other member. It records the returned error, the node's state, the in-memory latest configuration index and servers, and the last stored log index, then waits up to ten seconds for the node to be Leader again, applies one command with a three-second timeout, and emits the commit index, the leader's last log index and the other voter's last log index. The successor then shuts the phantom leader down, creates a fresh in-memory transport on the same address, calls NewRaft with the retained stores and its own config, waits up to ten seconds for Leader state, and emits phantom_restart with restart_ok, restarted_as_leader, leader_last_index, peer_last_index, lone_commit_retained and peer_caught_up. Before starting the restarted node, the harness connects the new transport to the peer's transport and repoints the peer's routing entry for the restarted address, so an election and replication can actually take place.
basis.responsibility: The library owns both the durability of a configuration change and the supporter set used for elections and commitment. A configuration entry that was never stored cannot be the configuration under which the node counts votes or commits entries; reporting the change as failed while adopting it for quorums leaves the caller and the cluster with incompatible views of who must agree.

comparisons.description: The failed log write must be reported to the caller as a failure.
The in-memory latest configuration must not refer to an index beyond the stored log.
A client command must not be reported committed unless the committed two-voter configuration's quorum, here both voters, has it; the peer lacking it contradicts this.
After restarting the phantom leader the peer should reach the lone commit so it becomes a real quorum commit; a peer that lags contradicts this.

semantic_changes: After the lone commit the harnes restarts the phantom leader from its own stores and records whether it regains leadership, whether the commit is retained and whether the peer catches up.
A new comparison asserts that the restarted peer has reached the lone commit's index.
The restarted node's fresh transport is connected to the surviving peer and the peer's routing entry is repointed to it, so the restart phase actually exercises recovery.
The restart phase's outcome is therefore attributable to the target rather than to missing transport wiring.

revision_reason: The restart phase in the previous revision created a fresh in-memory transport for the restarted node without connecting it to the peer, and left the peer's routing table pointing at the old transport, so its non-leadership result was a harness artifact. This revision connects the new transport to the peer in both directions and repoints the peer's entry before the election window; all other phases are unchanged.
